views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the existing Section 301 tariffs in place and continue intensive talks with Beijing without a new tariff hike, a unilateral rollback, or purchase concessions ahead of a signed text. Press for a written, two-way enforcement mechanism plus structural language on IP, forced tech transfer, and agriculture market access, and only schedule a Trump–Xi summit after those chapters are closed. Leave the Huawei/Meng legal track off the bargaining table rather than trading it for a weaker commercial deal.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The dispute is not an existential threat to US interests; it is a period of usable leverage. Lists 1–3 already cover ~$250B of Chinese imports, the scheduled List 3 hike from 10% to 25% has been deliberately held in reserve (delayed Feb 24 and again past the March 1 window), and China is still at the table after matching retaliation on ~$110B of US goods. April talks produced reported progress on text and enforcement offices, Mnuchin said the sides had “pretty much agreed” an enforcement mechanism and hoped they were near a “final round,” and Trump described an “epic” deal that was “very close” but still had “some way to go.” That is opportunity, not crisis: VIX is ~13, Michigan sentiment is back near 97, and 10-year yields have eased rather than signaling a trade-war recession. The reading is only a modest opportunity, not a clear one, because farm-belt costs are real (record soybean stocks, China buys still about a third of the pre-tariff run-rate, USDA aid already paying out billions), US industrial production has slipped ~1.7% over the window, and China’s Q1 GDP held at 6.4% with a March IP surprise of +8.5%, so Beijing is not overextended. Escalating now would risk blowing up the most constructive negotiating window since G20; conceding purchases or rolling back tariffs before enforcement and structural chapters are locked would repeat the May 2018 “trade war on hold” collapse. Negotiate without new commitments is therefore the stance that harvests leverage rather than spending it.
key_factors: Section 301 coverage still ~$250B with the List 3 10-to-25% hike held in reserve
April 2019 talks report progress on text and enforcement offices but no signed deal
US macro calm (VIX ~13, sentiment ~97) versus real but contained farm-export damage
China Q1 6.4% GDP and March IP rebound reduce the case that Beijing is desperate
Huawei/Meng extradition and Canadian detentions remain a separate legal/political overlay

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
Trump tweets that talks have made substantial progress and further delays the scheduled List 3 hike from 10% to 25%.
Intensive Washington talks; both sides report progress on text, including enforcement language. No final deal signed.
VIX latest 13.14 on 2019-04-24, down from 24.7 in late October — markets pricing calm, not crisis.
Michigan sentiment 97.2 in April 2019 after a January dip to 91.2.
US industrial production slipped from 104.07 (Nov 2018) to 102.27 (Apr 2019), about -1.7%.
US goods imports from China fell ~25.6% from $46.3B (Nov 2018) to $34.5B (Apr 2019).
Mnuchin: sides have “pretty much agreed on an enforcement mechanism” and will establish enforcement offices; important issues remain; no comment on removing $250B tariffs.
Mnuchin hoped talks were close to a “final round” of a seven-chapter deal with real two-way enforcement.
Trump: “some way to go” yet “very close”; Liu: “great progress”; China soybean commitments still about a third of pre-tariff US exports.
China Q1 2019 GDP +6.4%; March industrial production +8.5%, fastest since July 2014.
Record 3.7bn bushels of soybeans in storage; even pledged Chinese buys would leave a large overhang; $12bn farm aid softened 2018 blow.
